subject.title: [Bug]: agent-driven live update left a launchctl submit keepalive validator force-restarting the gateway every ~2 minutes

question: Should the remaining hardening stop at an explicit live-updater skill boundary, or should OpenClaw also broaden status/doctor detection to identify noncanonical `ai.openclaw.update-validator*` launchd jobs?
rationale: Existing release evidence covers stale updater-job detection, but treating arbitrary similarly named jobs as OpenClaw-owned changes the operator-facing diagnosis and cleanup boundary.

options.title: Add the skill boundary first
options.body: Explicitly prohibit persistent `launchctl submit` jobs and external restart watchdogs in the live-updater skill while retaining the existing managed-service diagnostics.

options.title: Broaden diagnostic matching
options.body: Also recognize the reported validator naming pattern, with clear non-destructive remediation guidance and tests for operator-owned-job false positives.

recommendation.title: Add the skill boundary first
recommendation.body: Explicitly prohibit persistent `launchctl submit` jobs and external restart watchdogs in the live-updater skill while retaining the existing managed-service diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed contributor connected to the existing stale-launchd-job diagnostic repair.
